summary.headline: UK SMEs face persistent cyber risks; sell practical readiness work before building a tool.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope cyber hygiene and incident-readiness setup for small UK businesses, with specialist referrals where needed.
summary.why_now: The 2025 DSIT Cyber Security Breaches Survey reports 43% of businesses identified a breach or attack in the prior year and estimates 612,000 businesses affected. This is evidence of a problem, not proof of willingness to buy from a new solo provider.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber hygiene and incident-readiness setup
top_opportunities.description: A fixed-scope review of backups, MFA, account access, update routines and incident contacts, followed by a prioritised action list and implementation help within competence; refer assurance or penetration testing to qualified partners.
top_opportunities.why_now: DSIT's 2025 survey estimates 612,000 businesses experienced breaches or attacks in the preceding year; 29% of businesses conducted cyber risk assessments overall, while small-business uptake rose to 48%.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-managed firms with 5–49 staff, especially professional services, property/administration and local service companies.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,000 for insurance, secure tooling, training and basic marketing; validate actual quotes before launch.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through direct referrals and a paid pilot; unvalidated estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Quarterly check-ins, staff awareness sessions and documented control reviews; do not imply formal certification.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a software engineer who can automate evidence collection and reporting; security competence and liability boundaries are critical.
risks: Trust, qualifications, professional indemnity and scope boundaries may impede sales.
Survey prevalence does not establish local buyer demand or price willingness; avoid overstating security assurance.

scores.competition: 3/5 — established IT providers and consultants; differentiate on clear fixed scope
scores.startup_ease: 4/5 — service-first, provided skills and insurance are adequate
scores.speed_to_cash: 4/5 — paid diagnostic is sellable before product development
scores.recurring_revenue: 3/5 — repeat reviews possible but must demonstrate ongoing value
scores.founder_fit: 4/5 — technical delivery fits; specialist security knowledge required

top_opportunities.verdict: Best near-term test: sell a tightly bounded readiness review, partner for specialist security work, and validate paid demand before productising.

top_opportunities.name: Workflow automation implementation for one SME niche
top_opportunities.description: Paid setup of a single repeatable workflow such as enquiry triage, quote follow-up or document processing using clients' existing systems and approved AI services.
top_opportunities.why_now: This run found no reliable live evidence establishing current UK SME AI purchasing intent; treat demand as a hypothesis and sell a measurable pilot.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small recruitment, property or professional-service firms with repetitive admin and an identifiable workflow owner.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£800 for hosting, APIs, demos and sales materials, excluding founder time.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks if sold as discovery plus implementation; estimate requiring validation.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monitoring, maintenance and iteration retainers where measurable workflow value persists.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical fit; requires disciplined scoping, privacy controls and support boundaries.
risks: Crowded market and generic AI claims make customer acquisition difficult.
Integration failures, data protection obligations and shifting third-party APIs can erode margins.

scores.demand: 3/5 — plausible pain, current buying signal unverified
scores.speed_to_cash: 4/5 — service can be sold before software exists
scores.recurring_revenue: 4/5 — maintenance can recur if outcomes are clear

top_opportunities.verdict: Test one narrow workflow with paid pilots; do not build a generic AI agency or SaaS first.

top_opportunities.name: SME backup and recovery readiness service
top_opportunities.description: Assess backup configuration and recovery procedures, help run a supervised restore test, and provide a recurring documented check using established backup vendors.
top_opportunities.why_now: DSIT's 2025 survey says 71% of businesses reported securely backing up data via a cloud service, leaving a potential readiness and verification gap; this does not prove independent-service demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small firms that depend on cloud files and lack internal IT staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,200 for insurance, secure test environment and training; exclude client backup subscriptions.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks for a fixed-price assessment if referrals or targeted outreach work; estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly or quarterly restore-test evidence and change review.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for technical operator; do not guarantee recovery or alter production without consent.
risks: Potential overlap with incumbent managed IT providers.
Misconfiguration or data loss creates substantial liability; require explicit authorization and safeguards.

scores.demand: 3/5 — backup adoption is widespread, unmet verification not directly measured

top_opportunities.verdict: A viable add-on to cyber readiness, but validate whether firms will pay independently of their MSP.

top_opportunities.name: Lead-response and booking automation for local service firms
top_opportunities.description: Connect website forms, email and booking tools to acknowledge enquiries, route leads and remind staff to follow up; report response and conversion metrics.
top_opportunities.why_now: Fast response has intuitive commercial value, but this run did not retrieve robust current UK evidence quantifying the opportunity; test a narrowly defined local vertical.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent trades, clinics or appointment-based businesses missing or delaying enquiries.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for demo tooling, domain and outreach; client software billed separately.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks for a paid setup if an owner confirms missed leads; unverified estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Hosting, monitoring and monthly conversion reporting.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong fit for web integrations; requires a reachable local sales channel.
risks: High churn if leads are low-volume or results cannot be attributed.
Messaging consent, personal data handling and platform dependencies require care.

scores.demand: 3/5 — obvious pain but no sourced demand measure in this run

top_opportunities.verdict: Sell a measurable one-business pilot before templating; target firms with demonstrable missed enquiries.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical micro-SaaS for compliance or operations
top_opportunities.description: A small workflow product for one underserved UK trade, such as inspection records, renewal reminders or evidence packs, initially delivered manually where possible.
top_opportunities.why_now: No sufficiently specific live signal for a particular underserved niche was verified in this run; opportunity depends on customer interviews, not a broad SaaS thesis.
top_opportunities.buyer: A tightly selected trade or small regulated-service segment with recurring paperwork and a reachable owner community.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £500–£2,000 for a narrow prototype, hosting and discovery; avoid paid development beyond the cap.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Usually slower than service work; seek paid design partners before building. Timeline uncertain.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription if the workflow is frequent, costly and retained over time.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High technical fit, but customer discovery and distribution are the main unknowns.
risks: Building before securing committed buyers can consume the full budget without revenue.
Established vertical software and compliance changes create product and support burden.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start with a build; get three paid commitments for one repetitive workflow first.

best_pick.name: SME cyber hygiene and incident-readiness setup
best_pick.why_it_wins: It pairs a recent official indicator of UK business exposure with a service-first offer that can generate revenue before software is built. Evidence supports the problem, not this offer's demand; validate buyer access and willingness to pay.
validation_plan: Interview 10 owner-managed firms or trusted IT/referral partners about risk reviews, backup restore tests and incident processes without fear-based selling.
Offer three paid, fixed-scope pilots with written boundaries; proceed only if buyers pay and delivery can be insured and competently performed.
best_pick.first_offer: A fixed-price cyber hygiene and incident-readiness review, with prioritised action plan and supervised backup-restore check only when explicitly authorised; quote after validating scope, insurance and local pricing.
best_pick.mvp: Secure checklist, evidence log and concise action report delivered manually using client-approved tools; no bespoke SaaS, penetration testing or certification claims.
customer_types: Small property, administration or local service businesses without internal IT staff
best_pick.do_today: Review DSIT's 2025 survey, define competence and insurance boundaries, then contact five trusted SME owners or IT referral partners for discovery conversations; do not make unsupported security claims.
